items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: like the people, well like Angela Davis and Sandra Lieb, who wrote those Ma Rainey books

ctx.x: Yes. Do you have to delve into the confusing world of copyrights and ownership and licensing when you get involved in re-issues?

I’m not really that involved in re-issues, but it’s kind of an impediment to study in a way because composer credits on record labels and often times on sheet music aren’t going to tell you what you want to know which is who actually wrote the song. Those credits are going to tell you how the money is being divided up when the publisher’s royalties come through. So people lean on those composer credits very heavily, like the people, well like Angela Davis and Sandra Lieb, who wrote those Ma Rainey books, they…

went in that direction. I mean those are distinctions we create because music composition has become a business instead of an art. And when there’s a business there’s money being made, and when there’s money being made you’ve got to decide how to divide it up and that’s really what those things are good for. So yes, I think composer credits are very important. I discovered fairly early on that if I looked at those on records that I didn’t know often times it would tell me — on jazz records especially — it would…
